title: Core components: LLM, tools, memory, planning
notes: An agent has four parts: a model that decides, tools, memory and planning.
The model only asks for a tool. Your code runs it and has the final say.
You build the model in Module 2, tools in 3, memory and planning in 4.

slides.title: Core components: LLM, tools, memory, planning
slides.sub: The four parts every agent is built from
sentences: So far, we have looked at agents from the outside.
Now let's open Scout up and look inside.
Every agent, from a small support bot to a coding assistant, is built from the same four parts, and you will build each one.

slides.title: Scout's four core parts

note.text: Model is the brain. Tools are hands, memory a notebook, planning a to-do list.

sentences: Here is Scout, with its four core parts around it.
The LLM, the language model, reads the conversation, decides what to do and writes the replies.
Tools let it look things up and take actions, like fetching an order.
Memory keeps what matters, like the customer's name and order number.
Planning breaks a request into steps and puts them in a sensible order.
Think of the model as the brain, and the other three as its hands, its notebook and its to-do list.

slides.title: Each part in one line

cells: Reads Ana's message, picks the next step
Still knows ORB-10482 ten messages later
Order, then stock, then offer a swap

note.text: You build them in order: LLM in Module 2, tools in 3, memory and planning in 4.

sentences: Now each part in one line, with Scout as the example.
The LLM understands Ana's message and picks a next step, such as looking up her order.
A tool does the looking up: the get order tool returns shipped, with a ParcelPath tracking number.
Memory means that ten messages later, Scout still knows which order Ana is talking about.
Planning means that for Owen's size swap, Scout checks his order, then the stock, and only then offers the swap.
You will build them in that order: the model in Module 2, tools in Module 3, and memory and planning in Module 4.

slides.title: How a tool call works

note.text: The model only asks. Your code decides what runs.

sentences: One detail surprises almost everyone, so let's get it right from day one.
For tools you define, the model never runs anything itself: it sends back a request naming the tool and its input.
Your own Python code receives that request and runs the real lookup.
The result goes back to the model as part of the conversation.
Then the model continues: it calls another tool, or writes the final reply.
This matters for safety, because your code always has the final say over what actually runs.

slides.title: Memory in a conversation

messages.label: Ana
messages.text: Hi, I'm Ana. Where's my order ORB-10482?

messages.label: Scout
messages.text: Hi Ana. Your Trailhead 2P tent has shipped with ParcelPath. Tracking: PP-88213.

messages.label: Ana
messages.text: Thanks. Can I send it back if it's not right?

messages.label: Scout
messages.text: Yes. Unused items in original packaging can go back within 30 days of delivery. Return shipping is free on your order.

aside.label: Without memory
aside.text: Scout would ask who she is and which order, all over again.

sentences: Memory is easiest to see in a conversation.
Ana introduces herself and gives her order number.
Scout looks the order up and answers.
Then she asks a follow-up, without repeating her order number.
Scout still knows which order she means, and that it is over seventy-five dollars, so return shipping is free.
Without memory, every message would start from zero, and Ana would have to explain herself all over again.

slides.title: Planning: Owen's size swap
slides.scenario: Owen: My storm shell jacket in L is too big. Can I swap it for an M?

steps.text: Look up ORB-10588: jacket, size L, delivered 5 days ago
Policy: size swaps are free if the new size is in stock
Offer the free swap and explain next steps

result.text: Four steps in a sensible order, chosen by Scout, not scripted.

sentences: Planning shows up when a request needs more than one step.
Owen says his storm jacket in large is too big, and asks to swap it for a medium.
Scout plans its steps, starting with his order, which was delivered five days ago.
Next it checks the policy: swapping sizes is free if the new size is in stock.
Then it checks the stock, and there are three mediums left.
Only then does it offer the free swap, and explain what happens next.
Nobody wrote those four steps in advance; Scout worked out the order from the request.

aside.label: Any provider
aside.text: Other providers use the same four ideas. This course uses Anthropic's SDK.

sentences: Here is a quick look at how each part shows up in code.
The LLM is a single call to the messages create method, with the model's name.
Tools are a list of definitions you pass in, so the model knows what it may ask for.
Memory, at its simplest, is the list of messages you keep adding to.
And the loop that lets Scout plan and act runs inside a step limit, so it can never run forever.
The ideas are the same with any provider, including OpenAI, Google and open models; this course uses Anthropic's SDK.

slides.title: What to take away

points.text: Four parts: the LLM, tools, memory and planning
The model asks for a tool, and your code runs it
Memory keeps context. Planning orders the steps
You'll build each part, starting in Module 2

sentences: Time to recap.
Every agent has four parts: the model, tools, memory and planning.
The model only asks for a tool, and your code runs it and sends the result back.
Memory keeps the conversation and key facts, and planning puts the steps in order.
You will build each part, starting with the model in Module 2.
But first, one more lesson: getting your machine ready.

midQuiz.q: Which part decides what to do next?
midQuiz.explain: The language model reads the conversation and decides. Tools act, and memory holds context.
midQuiz.hint: Which part did we call the brain?

endQuiz.q: For Owen's swap, Scout checks his order, then the policy, then stock. Which part chose that order?
endQuiz.explain: Planning breaks a request into ordered steps. Tools do each lookup, and memory keeps what was learned.
endQuiz.hint: Which part did we call the to-do list?

The messages list that grows each turn
